description: Stucco crack repair, patching, and elastomeric painting in Gainesville, Ocala, and North Central Florida. We diagnose the crack before we coat it.
h1: Stucco Repair and Painting for Florida Homes and Buildings

sections.h2: Stucco in North Central Florida takes a beating
body: Stucco over block or frame is everywhere from Ocala subdivisions to Gainesville infill homes. It is durable, but it is not waterproof by itself. Paint is what keeps rain out of the cement, and once cracks open or the coating chalks away, water gets in, mildew grows, and the wall starts to deteriorate. Stucco repair and painting is the fix, and it works best when the repair and the coating are planned as one system.

Common signs that a stucco wall is due include chalky residue that rubs off on your hand, green or black mildew streaks under eaves, hairline cracks fanning out from window corners, and paint bubbling near the ground where sprinklers hit. Any one of those is a reason to have the wall looked at before the next rainy season, because small cracks that let water in during summer storms tend to grow.

We handle stucco on single-family homes, villas and townhomes, small commercial buildings, and site walls. For associations repainting many buildings at once, the same repair approach is built into our HOA and property management painting scopes.

sections.h2: Reading the cracks before repairing them
body: Not every crack means the same thing, so the first step on the walkthrough is sorting them:
bullets: Map or spider cracking: fine shrinkage cracks across the surface, usually cosmetic and bridged by a high-build coating
Straight cracks off window and door corners: stress cracks that need to be opened, filled with flexible sealant, and texture patched
Stair-step cracks following block joints: a sign of movement that should be evaluated before paint covers it
Cracks around penetrations, hose bibs, and light fixtures: water entry points that need sealing
Hollow-sounding or bulging areas: stucco that has lost bond and must be cut out and replaced

body: Stress cracks are routed out into a clean channel so the sealant has room to flex, then filled with a paintable elastomeric sealant. Larger damaged areas are cut back to sound material and patched with a compatible stucco mix, then textured to match the surrounding wall, whether that is sand finish, skip trowel, or smooth. Texture is the part that makes a patch disappear or stand out, so crews practice the match on the wall before committing.

Control joints, window perimeters, and wall penetrations are re-caulked as part of the scope. Our guide on hiding stucco cracks goes deeper into why patches flash through and how to avoid it, and homeowners up north may find our post on stucco cracks in Lake City homes useful.

sections.h2: Moisture first, then the right coating
body: Stucco needs to release moisture outward. If a damp wall is sealed under a coating that cannot breathe, the water has nowhere to go and the result is blistering, peeling, and white mineral bloom. Before coating, the crew takes moisture readings on suspect areas and looks for the source: sprinklers spraying the wall, missing kickout flashing at a roofline, or a failed window seal.

For walls with hairline movement, we typically specify an elastomeric coating, a thick, flexible film that stretches over small cracks and sheds wind-driven rain. On sound stucco without active cracking, a premium 100% acrylic masonry paint may be the better fit because it breathes more readily. Both come from Sherwin-Williams or Benjamin Moore lines, and the product is named on your estimate. Two full coats is the baseline, applied after washing and a masonry primer where needed.

The walls are soft washed to remove dirt, chalk, and mildew. Crack and patch repairs come next and are allowed to cure. Joints are sealed, bare patches are primed, and the coating is applied by spray and back-rolled so it works into the texture. A full exterior usually runs three to seven working days plus washing and dry time, and October through May is the most comfortable window.

Exterior work includes a written workmanship warranty of up to 10 years on top of the manufacturer's warranty. Stucco repair is often one part of a larger exterior painting project that includes trim, doors, and fascia. For bare block that was never stuccoed, see concrete and masonry painting.

After the job, keep sprinkler heads pointed away from the walls, rinse mildew from shaded sides once or twice a year, and check sealant at windows every few seasons. Small cracks caught early can be sealed and touched up with the labelled paint we leave behind.

faqs.q: Is elastomeric paint always the right choice for stucco?
faqs.a: Not always. It is excellent on walls with hairline cracking, but on sound stucco a breathable 100% acrylic masonry paint can perform better. We decide after checking cracks and moisture.

faqs.q: Will the patches show after painting?
faqs.a: Patches are textured to match before coating, and two coats unify the wall. Texture matching is what keeps repairs from flashing through.

faqs.q: Why is my stucco paint blistering?
faqs.a: Usually moisture trapped behind the coating, often from sprinklers, flashing gaps, or window leaks. The source has to be fixed before the wall is recoated.

faqs.q: Do you repair large sections of stucco?
faqs.a: We cut out and patch damaged or delaminated areas as part of a paint project. Structural movement should be evaluated by the appropriate professional first, and we will tell you when we see it.
